claims.statement: A quality improvement study at Houston Methodist Hospital compared artificial intelligence discharge-date estimates with contemporaneous case-manager estimates across the hospital stay.
claims.value_text: Two estimate types were compared: artificial intelligence and case manager.
claims.quote: This quality improvement study included inpatient encounters at Houston Methodist Hospital with discharge dates between August 1, 2023, and February 28, 2024. We compared the accuracy of an artificial intelligence (AI)–generated discharge date with contemporaneous, independently generated case manager estimates and both estimates with the true discharge date across the hospital course.
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients

claims.statement: In the analysis labeled 24 hours, case managers placed more estimates within one day of the real date than the artificial intelligence tool did; the methods defined that checkpoint as the first estimate recorded in a 12-to-36-hour window before discharge.
claims.value_text: At 24 hours, 79.5% of case-manager estimates fell within 1 day versus 37.9% of artificial-intelligence estimates.
claims.quote: We assessed estimations at 3 time points: admission (first available estimate per method) and 48 and 24 hours before discharge (first estimate in a symmetric window 36-60 and 12-36 hours before true discharge, applied identically to both methods). At 24 hours, 79.5% of case manager estimations fell within 1 day vs 37.9% for AI estimations.
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients

claims.statement: Closer to discharge, case managers had lower mean absolute error than the artificial intelligence tool at both later checkpoints.
claims.quote: Nearer to discharge, case managers vs AI were more accurate (48 hours: MAE, 1.29 [95% CI, 1.26-1.32] vs 1.59 [95% CI 1.57-1.61] days; 24 hours: MAE, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.96-1.01] vs 1.93 [95% CI, 1.91-1.95] days) (both P < .001).
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients

claims.statement: At admission the methods were close on error, while case managers matched the exact date and landed within one day more often.
claims.quote: At admission, accuracy was similar between methods (MAE, 4.20 [95% CI, 4.08-4.31] vs 4.27 [4.15-4.38] days; P = .001), although case managers matched the exact date more often (23.6% vs 15.3%) and fell within 1 day more often (46.3% vs 40.8%).
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients

claims.statement: The artificial intelligence dates came from a commercial clinician-assisted tool integrated with the electronic health record.
claims.quote: Artificial intelligence–estimated discharge dates were generated by a commercial clinician-assisted tool integrated with the EHR.
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients

claims.statement: The authors found the artificial intelligence estimate comparable at admission and outperformed by case managers near discharge, when accurate estimates are most actionable for bed management.
claims.quote: This quality improvement study found that AI-estimated discharge was comparable to usual care at admission but outperformed by case managers as discharge approached (when accurate estimations are most actionable for bed management).
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients

claims.statement: The authors warn that admission correlation should not be treated as evidence that the tool captured the information clinicians used across the stay.
claims.quote: The strong admission correlation did not persist nearer discharge and should not be interpreted as evidence that the tool captured the same information clinicians use throughout the stay.
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients

claims.statement: The study says case-manager estimates were visible to care teams and may have been partly self-fulfilling, while artificial intelligence estimates were available in the record but not automatically enabled.
claims.quote: Case manager estimates were part of usual care and visible to care teams, so they may be partly self-fulfilling and, thus, advantaged nearer discharge; AI estimations were accessible in the EHR but not enabled automatically.
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients

claims.statement: The authors call for prospective outcome-based evaluation before deciding whether the tool's subgroup accuracy is worth the implementation complexity.
claims.quote: Whether the AI's incremental accuracy in selected subgroups justifies the complexity of implementation warrants prospective, outcome-based evaluation.
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients

claims.statement: The study was published in JAMA Network Open on September 3rd, 2026.
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients

claims.statement: This single-center analysis measured estimation accuracy, not downstream clinical decisions or patient outcomes, so the authors describe the findings as hypothesis-generating.
claims.quote: This single-center analysis assessed estimation accuracy, not downstream clinical decisions or patient outcomes; thus, the findings are hypothesis-generating.
claims.source_title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Discharge Dates and Estimation Accuracy in Hospitalized Patients

rejected.finding: The paper identifies a specific product vendor.
rejected.reason: The verified text supports only the description commercial clinician-assisted tool integrated with the electronic health record, so no vendor is named in the film.

rejected.finding: The comparison proves the artificial intelligence tool cannot improve hospital outcomes.
rejected.reason: The study compares estimation accuracy, raises a workflow confound, and explicitly calls for prospective outcome-based evaluation.
